title: Make offline exercise recovery explicit
goal_md: Give a learner an honest way to restore or discard offline progress while preserving the last known good state.

included: Restore, discard, and unavailable-state recovery flows

constraints.text_md: Show saved only after the persistence operation succeeds; a failed write must preserve the previous valid snapshot.
An invalid local snapshot is unavailable, not silently treated as an empty exercise session.
Starting over invalidates queued saves from the discarded session so an older write cannot resurrect progress.

phases.title: Persist completed exercises and outcomes
phases.objective_md: Callers can distinguish saved, unsaved, unavailable, restored, and discarded outcomes without guessing from a notification.
phases.approach_md: Keep snapshot reads and writes behind a small session boundary. Return an explicit outcome only after the write completes, retain the prior valid snapshot after a failure, and fence queued writes when a session is discarded.

acceptance_criteria.text_md: A completed exercise reports saved only after its snapshot write succeeds.
A failed write reports unsaved and leaves the previous valid progress available for restore.
Malformed or incompatible local data produces an explicit unavailable result instead of an empty valid session.
After starting over, a queued save from the discarded session cannot publish progress into the new session.

phases.title: Explain restore and start-over choices
phases.objective_md: The recovery surface makes the available snapshot and each consequence clear before the learner chooses restore or start over.
phases.approach_md: Use a compact recovery panel with explicit result labels, a visibly illustrative prototype, and a fallback when the snapshot is unavailable. Keep the persistence outcomes from the preceding phase visible in the UI contract.

acceptance_criteria.text_md: A recoverable snapshot clearly identifies the exact progress that Restore will return
Start over explains that the stored snapshot and any queued session work are discarded.
An unavailable snapshot uses the wording ‘This offline progress is unavailable. You can start over.’ and gives a safe path without pretending restoration succeeded.

references.purpose_md: Retained narrative explaining the state transitions represented by the package.

decisions.title: Persistence returns named outcomes
decisions.decision_md: The recovery experience consumes named outcomes rather than inferring persistence from a generic success toast.
decisions.rationale_md: A visible saved state must be trustworthy when writes can fail or arrive out of order.

decisions.title: Prototype behavior is visibly simulated
decisions.decision_md: The selected recovery prototype labels its controls and outcomes as mock behavior and does not claim to persist an exercise.

decisions.title: Unavailable state uses direct learner-facing wording
decisions.decision_md: Use the learner-facing wording ‘This offline progress is unavailable. You can start over.’ Reserve ‘could not be restored’ for a specific restore failure.
decisions.rationale_md: Direct state language tells the learner what is unavailable and gives a safe next action without implying that restoration succeeded.

questions.title: Choose the learner-facing unavailable wording
questions.question_md: Resolved: use the learner-facing wording ‘This offline progress is unavailable. You can start over.’ Reserve ‘could not be restored’ for a specific restore failure.
